title: Dragging the side edge of a one line text box moves it instead of resizing it
goal: Put a label on the canvas, then take hold of its right edge and pull it in to make the words wrap. The label slides across the canvas instead: the edge only becomes a resize handle once the box is tall enough, so on the one line labels that most UI work is made of there is no way to set the wrap width by dragging. Corner handles still resize, and so does the bottom edge of a tall box.
notes:
REPRODUCED 2026-09-09 with the probe build, on clean main plus the text-height-readout walk fix.

A text layer at 140,140 pinned to W 360 is 29pt tall, so its box is x 140-500, y 140-169.

  drag (500, 140) -> (250, 140)  cursor while down resize-up-right-down-left   W 360 -> 110, H 29 -> 113   (top right CORNER: resizes)
  drag (500, 150) -> (250, 150)  cursor while down arrow                        X 140 -> -110, W 360         (right EDGE: moves)
  drag (499, 154) -> (250, 154)  cursor while down arrow                        no resize                    (right edge, exact middle: moves)

Same layer with H typed to 120, so the box is 120pt tall:

  drag (500, 200) -> (400, 200)  cursor while down resize-left-right                                         (right EDGE: resizes)

So the side handle exists and is simply not reachable on a short box: the two corner handles claim the whole 29pt edge between them. Scripts/playtest/text-box-room-walk.json drags the BOTTOM edge of a tall box and gets resize-up-down, which is the same handle family working where there is room for it.

Fallout in the walks: text-width-floor-walk drags from (272, 150), the middle of a 21pt tall box edge, and describes it as the right edge dragged as far left as it will go. It moves the label; the walk passes and proves nothing about the 80pt floor. text-height-readout-walk had the same fiction and was changed on 2026-09-09 to drag the top right corner instead, which does re-wrap.

The fix is probably in the handle hit testing for a short box (give the side handles the middle of the edge, or shrink the corner claim on a box under about 40pt), not in the walks.
acceptance: Dragging the right or left edge of a one line text box resizes it and re-wraps the words, with the pointer showing the left-right resize cursor
Dragging the middle of the same label still moves it

Scripts/playtest/text-width-floor-walk.json actually narrows the label: its stage 2 note claims the drag stops at 80 wide and today the label just moves, so the walk needs to prove the floor rather than assert it

log.note: Adversarial review of the fix before building it. The obvious fix — let the side midpoint square come back on a short box — does not work: on a 29pt tall label the square sits 19.5pt from each corner, and on the 21pt label the width floor walk uses it sits 15.5pt away, which is a 7pt gap between 8pt squares. That is the lattice the cramped rule exists to prevent, and the line between 'works' and 'lattice' would fall between a 21pt label and a 16pt one, which is not a rule anyone can predict. So the handle stops being a square: the whole run of an EDGE answers to a press, which is what Figma and Sketch do and why their short boxes have sides you can pull. Trade-offs weighed: (1) no square is drawn on a short box's side, so the invitation is the pointer turning into resize arrows rather than something visible at rest — accepted, that is the platform idiom; (2) a selected layer loses its outer 6pt ring as a move target, so an edge band may only exist while 20 clear points survive down the middle of the box on that axis, which on a one line label switches the top and bottom edges OFF and keeps the whole body grabbable; (3) the corner-radius dots sit 12pt in, clear of the band, and are read first anyway. Shortest version considered and rejected: side edges on text layers only. The same problem hits any short box (a divider, a 24pt button), and a rule that applies to one content type is unguessable.

Built. Handles.grabRun + Handles.hit(edgeGrab:) in PhotonzCore, behind next-edge-grab (on by default in Next, absent from Current's catalog so Current is untouched). Threaded through every press and hover site: layer handles, the crop box, the canvas boundary. Drawing is unchanged. Tests written first: EdgeGrabTests in Tests/PhotonzCoreTests/HandleLayoutTests.swift, 13 cases. Scripts/test.sh green: 5291 tests in 439 suites.

The whole run of a picked box's edge now resizes it (Handles.grabRun + Handles.hit(edgeGrab:) in PhotonzCore, behind next-edge-grab, on by default in Next). A one line label's sides set the wrap width; its body still moves it; a box with no room to spare offers no edges and moves from everywhere. Tests first (EdgeGrabTests, 13 cases); Scripts/test.sh green at 5291 tests. Verified in the probe: text-side-edge-walk drags the right edge of a 360 wide one line label to 110 with cursor resize-left-right and X unmoved at 140, then drags the middle and X travels to 240 with W unchanged. text-width-floor-walk was claiming the 80 point floor while dragging from INSIDE the label and only moving it; it now grabs the real edge and lands on 80. 29 walks across text, resize, move, crop, canvas and handles pass. Audit: queue/audits/2026-09-09-edge-grab.json. Commit 8a212ac2.
